s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-five. Economics optional, Paper One, fifteen marks. Define money multiplier and discuss its determinants. Then explain how the banking system can control money supply. Here's the trap. The formula most people write first is only true in a world with no cash.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Define means a precise meaning, with the formula. Discuss means more than one side. So there are three jobs: the definition, the determinants, and how the system controls money.

s003.text: Start with what NCERT shows. A bank must keep part of each deposit as reserves. Say twenty percent. A hundred rupees comes in. Eighty is lent, and comes back as a deposit somewhere else. Then sixty-four is lent, and so on.

s004.text: Add up the rounds, and a hundred rupees of reserves supports five hundred rupees of deposits. That five is the money multiplier. Here it is one over the reserve ratio.

s005.text: But people also keep cash. Every rupee held as cash stops a round. So the full formula has two ratios: cash to deposits, and reserves to deposits. In India, cash is about fifteen percent of deposits.

s006.text: Now we write. No word limit is printed, so we set our own: about two hundred and fifty words in eleven minutes. Open with the definition in one line: the money supply is the multiplier times high-powered money.

s007.text: Section one gives the formula, and the case with no cash. Then a small diagram of the lending rounds. It takes a minute, and it proves you understand.

s008.text: Section two is the determinants. The reserve ratio, which RBI sets partly through the CRR, now three percent. The public's taste for cash. Banks' willingness to lend. And shocks: in the Great Depression, people pulled cash from banks, and America's money shrank.

s009.text: Section three answers the control question. RBI changes high-powered money by buying or selling bonds. It changes the reserve ratio. And today its main lever is the policy rate. Banks create deposits when they lend, so the multiplier is a limit, not a constant.

s010.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It writes one over CRR, and stops. It says today's multiplier is about thirty-three. It lists only CRR and SLR. It never says how control works. And there is no worked example.

s011.text: Here is the payoff. One frame answers its cousins. Twenty eighteen asked about high-powered money. Twenty nineteen asked what happens when people hoard cash. Twenty twenty-four asked about credit creation. Learn the frame once. For the full story of how banks create money, watch our money episode.
